what_its_for: Pomalidomide is a cancer medicine used to treat multiple myeloma (a type of blood cancer) in adults who have already tried at least two other treatments that did not work well enough. It is sometimes also used for a rare disease called Kaposi sarcoma. It works by helping your immune system fight cancer cells and by cutting off the blood supply that tumors need to grow.
how_to_take: Take pomalidomide capsules by mouth once a day on Days 1 through 21 of each 28-day treatment cycle. Swallow the capsules whole — do not open, break, or chew them. You can take this medicine with or without food. Take it at about the same time each day. Do not take more than your doctor prescribed. Because this medicine can cause serious birth defects, it is only available through a special safety program called POMALYST REMS. You must be enrolled in this program to receive the medicine.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 4 mg taken once daily on Days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects or certain health conditions such as kidney problems. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your usual time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next day. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pomalidomide capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C–25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep the capsules in the original packaging until you are ready to take them. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do NOT flush unused capsules down the toilet or throw them in the trash. Return any unused capsules to the pharmacy or follow the special disposal instructions in the POMALYST REMS program.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or could become pregnant — it causes very serious, life-threatening birth defects. All patients must use required birth control methods throughout treatment and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose. Male patients must always use a condom during sexual activity. Do not donate blood, sperm, or eggs while taking this medicine and for at least 4 weeks after stopping. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and St. John's Wort, as they may affect how the medicine works. Avoid smoking, as it may reduce the effectiveness of treatment. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: shortness of breath, chest pain, or leg swelling or pain (possible blood clots); fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bleeding or easy bruising; dizziness, fainting, or confusion; severe rash, blistering, or peeling skin; numbness or tingling in hands or feet; feeling very tired or weak; yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice); or if you think you or your partner may be pregnant. These could be signs of serious side effects that need immediate medical attention.
when_it_works: Pomalidomide does not work overnight. Most patients begin to see a response within the first few treatment cycles, but it may take several weeks or months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular blood tests and check-ups. Even if you feel well, continue taking the medicine as directed unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine MUST NOT be used during pregnancy. It causes life-threatening birth defects. A negative pregnancy test is required before starting treatment and regularly during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Kidney problems: If you are on dialysis, your dose may be adjusted and you should take the medicine after each dialysis session. Liver problems: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor you closely and may adjust your dose. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects such as fatigue, infections, and blood clots, so close monitoring is important. Children: This medicine has not been approved for use in children.
